subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should OpenClaw memory status truth come from the live gateway runtime, a passive local plugin status contract, or remain `not checked` unless an explicit full status scan runs?
rationale: Current code partially mitigates the old wording but leaves a product/API boundary choice between live gateway truth and local plugin materialization, and an open conflicting closing PR is already attached to this issue.

options.title: Define live-gateway runtime health
options.body: Expose runtime health separately from embedding readiness in `doctor.memory.status` and use it for human and JSON status when local memory materialization is inconclusive.

options.title: Define passive local plugin status
options.body: Keep status local but require a passive plugin status API that cannot run heavyweight startup or mutate state, then update plugin/runtime contracts and tests.

options.title: Leave as not checked
options.body: Keep the current conservative output and close or supersede the open fix PRs only after documenting that `status --deep` is not a live memory health check.

recommendation.title: Define live-gateway runtime health
recommendation.body: Expose runtime health separately from embedding readiness in `doctor.memory.status` and use it for human and JSON status when local memory materialization is inconclusive.

likelyOwner.reason: The memory-runtime-through-plugin refactor and status memory surface history make this the strongest routing candidate for the product/API boundary decision.
